scope.definition: Autonomous coding agent platforms are products or deployable agents that accept a repository-level goal, inspect code, execute tools in a development environment, edit multiple files, run verification, and hand back a branch or pull request. This item covers the issue/prompt-to-reviewed-PR stage, not autonomous product strategy, unrestricted production deployment, generic autocomplete, dependency bots, or a full survey of open-source orchestration frameworks [S01,S09,S13,S17].
systems_in_depth: Cognition Devin (hosted cloud plus terminal/desktop surfaces and API)
OpenAI Codex cloud plus local CLI/IDE surfaces
GitHub Copilot cloud agent (formerly coding agent), including GitHub-hosted Claude and Codex partner agents
Anthropic Claude Code local/web plus GitHub Actions
scope.time_boundary: Developments from 2019 through 2026-09-13, with SWE-bench (2023/2024) as a benchmark foundation. Product state is the live documentation visible on 2026-09-13; undated docs are not treated as historical proof.

current_state.claim: All four leading families can perform the bounded loop repo checkout/index -> plan -> edit -> shell/test -> diff/branch -> human review, asynchronously in cloud or interactively on a developer machine [S01,S09,S10,S13,S17,S19].

Triggering has moved beyond chat: GitHub issues/PR comments and agent panels, Slack/Linear/Jira-style integrations, APIs, schedules and repository events can start work; Devin v3 exposes RBAC service users and session APIs, Claude exposes Actions/Agent SDK patterns, and GitHub cloud-agent automations can react to events [S03,S08,S09,S13,S16,S19,S23].

Hosted agents normally isolate work in ephemeral containers/VMs and hand off a branch or draft PR. GitHub explicitly prevents its cloud agent from approving/merging and gates workflow execution; Codex blocks agent internet by default; Cursor describes an isolated-VM-to-draft-PR lifecycle [S10,S11,S14,S24].

The solved unit is a well-scoped, testable engineering task, not unattended ownership of an evolving product. Vendors themselves recommend explicit criteria, easy verification, decomposition, and short/small tasks; external tests show large outcome variance [S01,S05,S06,S28].

Automated issue triage, confidence thresholds, fleets/parallel sessions, automatic review fixes and cross-repository work exist, but important pieces remain preview, vendor-specific, or only workflow conveniences rather than enforceable security boundaries [S08,S15,S16,S23].

representative_systems.status_as_of: GA since 2024-12-10; current docs expose cloud, Slack/Teams, Linear/Jira, CLI/desktop/IDE handoff, GitHub integration, v3 organization/enterprise APIs and analytics [S01,S03,S05].
representative_systems.best_fit: parallel, clear and mechanically verifiable backlog work; migrations, security fixes, tests and small tickets [S01,S06].
representative_systems.material_limit: vendor describes senior codebase understanding but junior execution; requires decomposition/coaching and review [S05,S06].

representative_systems.status_as_of: available cloud service with GitHub and GitLab (Beta) repository connections and GitHub/GitLab/Linear/Slack starting points; local CLI/IDE also available [S09,S10].
representative_systems.best_fit: parallel isolated tasks in reproducible environments, with AGENTS.md and post-run diff/follow-up [S09,S10].
representative_systems.material_limit: useful setup often needs custom scripts; agent network is off by default and enabling it adds injection/exfiltration/dependency risks [S10,S11].

representative_systems.status_as_of: native GitHub asynchronous agent; can research, plan, change a branch, optionally open a PR, and run scheduled/event automations. Claude and Codex partner agents were still public preview in GitHub documentation [S13,S15,S16].
representative_systems.best_fit: organizations whose issues, rulesets, Actions, security scanning, review and audit already live on GitHub [S13,S14].
representative_systems.material_limit: consumes Actions plus AI credits; deep research/plan-first behavior is not uniform across every integration, and partner/automation features may be preview [S13,S15,S16].

representative_systems.status_as_of: agentic terminal, IDE, desktop, browser/web and GitHub Action; fine-grained permissions, sandboxing, hooks, SDK and OTel [S17-S21].
representative_systems.best_fit: developer-driven local work or custom CI/issue-to-PR pipelines needing programmable hooks and provider/deployment flexibility [S19-S21].
representative_systems.material_limit: local mode runs near valuable credentials and files unless policy/sandbox rules are engineered; automation cost varies strongly with model, context and concurrency [S18,S20,S22].

representative_systems.status_as_of: hosted isolated VMs, parallel and multi-repo environments, GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/Azure DevOps, Slack/Linear/API and draft-PR handoff [S23,S24].
representative_systems.best_fit: teams already using Cursor that need background, browser-capable or multi-repo work.
representative_systems.material_limit: broad VM/MCP/network capability expands credential and exfiltration surface; human draft-PR review remains the principal gate [S23,S24].

representative_systems.status_as_of: asynchronous GitHub coding agent, out of public beta since 2025-08-06, although its live getting-started page still calls it experimental [S25,S26].
representative_systems.best_fit: GitHub-centric users wanting a simple hosted alternative.
representative_systems.material_limit: the public-beta/experimental wording conflict signals evolving maturity and documentation semantics [S25,S26].

representative_systems.status_as_of: active open-source repository with local/self-hostable and hosted routes [S27].
representative_systems.best_fit: organizations needing inspectable/extensible orchestration or self-hosting.
representative_systems.material_limit: the buyer owns sandbox hardening, model/provider selection, reliability engineering, upgrades and operations [S27].

primary_evidence.claim: Devin officially says it writes, runs and tests code, supports parallel sessions and multiple integrations, but advises clear completion criteria, easy verification and scoped work [S01,S05].
primary_evidence.classification: vendor documentation and guidance, not independent success proof

primary_evidence.claim: Devin v3 separates organization and enterprise scopes, supports RBAC service users, audit/session attribution, API-triggered sessions and usage controls [S03].
Codex cloud provisions a container, checks out a selected revision, runs setup, applies network policy, loops over terminal/edit/check operations, then presents answer and diff [S10].
Codex removes configured secrets after setup before the agent phase and blocks agent internet by default; optional allowlists and HTTP-method limits exist [S10,S11].
primary_evidence.classification: verified documented safeguard; not proof against every channel

primary_evidence.claim: GitHub cloud agent uses an Actions-powered ephemeral environment, one working branch and PR workflow; only write users can trigger, it cannot approve/merge, and Actions require approval by default [S13,S14].
GitHub scans agent output with CodeQL, secret scanning and dependency advisory checks and exposes signed commits, session links and audit logs [S14,S15].
primary_evidence.classification: verified documented controls; scanners have coverage limits

primary_evidence.claim: Claude Code manual mode starts read-only and asks on edits/commands, while sandbox policy enforces filesystem/network boundaries; GitHub Action turns @claude or events into repository work [S18-S20].

GitHub issue automation can record rationale and high/medium/low confidence and hold actions below a configured threshold, but GitHub explicitly says this approval UI is not a security boundary [S16].
primary_evidence.classification: verified preview behavior and explicit limitation

independent_evidence.result: Answer.AI used Devin for 20 heterogeneous tasks in Dec 2024/Jan 2025: 3 succeeded, 14 failed and 3 were inconclusive. Reviewers found success hard to predict and preferred more developer-steered tools [S28].
independent_evidence.caveat: Small purposive sample, old Devin generation, unusual nbdev/FastHTML-heavy tasks; strong qualitative failure evidence, not a current population success rate.

independent_evidence.result: METR randomized 246 real tasks from 16 experienced maintainers; early-2025 AI (mainly Cursor with Claude 3.5/3.7) increased completion time 19%, even though developers estimated a 20% speedup [S29].
independent_evidence.caveat: Measures synchronous experienced-maintainer work on mature repositories, not primarily unattended cloud agents or 2026 systems.

independent_evidence.result: METR’s 2026 update had raw point estimates of 18% speedup for returning developers and 4% for new recruits, but both confidence intervals crossed zero; opt-out, task selection, lower compensation and concurrent-agent timing made the authors call the signal unreliable [S30].
independent_evidence.caveat: Useful direction/conflict, not a valid current productivity estimate.

independent_evidence.result: SWE-Lancer used over 1,400 paid freelance tasks. On its Diamond split Claude 3.5 Sonnet resolved 26.2% of independent coding tasks and 44.9% of management choices; authors said most solutions remained incorrect [S33].
independent_evidence.caveat: 2025 models/scaffolds and benchmark grading; not a production platform comparison.

independent_evidence.result: SWE-rebench built 21,000+ continuously collected tasks and reported that some model scores on static SWE-bench Verified may be inflated by contamination [S32].
independent_evidence.caveat: Python-focused and performance depends on agent harness, budget and task vintage.

independent_evidence.result: AgentDojo’s 97 tasks/629 security cases show tool-using agents can fail without attacks and existing attacks/defenses do not secure all properties [S34].
independent_evidence.caveat: General tool-agent benchmark, not specific coding-platform red-team certification.

vendor_reported.metric: Devin: 67% of PRs merged versus 34% the previous year; 4x faster problem solving and 2x resource efficiency [S06].
vendor_reported.interpretation: Vendor aggregate; denominator, task routing, review policy and counterfactual human cost are not fully specified. Merge rate is selection- and workflow-dependent.

vendor_reported.metric: Cognition reports hundreds of thousands of merged Devin PRs and 659 Devin PRs merged internally in one week [S06,S08].
vendor_reported.interpretation: Evidence of scale and process integration, not correctness, net productivity or independent ROI.

vendor_reported.metric: Cognition productivity estimator reports log-scale correlation r_log=0.74 against human estimates [S07].
vendor_reported.interpretation: Promising aggregation tool but human-time-equivalent is not business value and individual predictions are imperfect.

vendor_reported.metric: Anthropic documents average enterprise Claude Code cost around $13 per active developer-day and $150–250/month, with 90% below $30 per active day [S22].
vendor_reported.interpretation: Vendor observational billing guidance; depends on models, context and automation.

independent.metric: Answer.AI Devin sample: 15% success, 70% failure, 15% inconclusive (3/20, 14/20, 3/20) [S28].
independent.interpretation: Old small sample; do not extrapolate to 2026.

independent.metric: METR early-2025 RCT: 19% slower; developers perceived 20% faster; n=16 developers, 246 tasks [S29].
independent.interpretation: Causal for that narrow setting, not all agentic workflows.

independent.metric: METR later raw estimates: 18% speedup returning and 4% new developers, with CIs -38% to +9% and -15% to +9%; authors judge unreliable [S30].
independent.interpretation: Shows improvement may have occurred but cannot quantify it.

independent.metric: SWE-bench original: 2,294 issues/12 Python repos; Claude 2 resolved 1.96% [S31]. SWE-Lancer Diamond IC best reported 26.2% [S33].
independent.interpretation: Capability rose sharply by 2025, yet majority failure on a more economic task distribution remained.

metrics.economic_rule: Measure accepted engineering hours, review/rework, CI minutes, inference/credits, incidents and lead time. Never use token volume, lines changed, PR count or vendor merge rate alone [S07,S13,S22].

reference_workflow.trigger: Issue created/labelled, scheduled maintenance event, failing CI/security alert, or approved human/API request.
reference_workflow.mechanics: A deterministic router checks repository allowlist, requester trust, task class, risk tier, estimated budget and whether acceptance tests exist. Untrusted public issue text is data, never authority [S11,S14,S16,S34].
reference_workflow.output: task envelope with source URL, target SHA, owner, risk tier, budget and deadline.

reference_workflow.mechanics: Generate a bounded plan and ask for clarification if behavior, acceptance criteria, interfaces or migrations are ambiguous. Require reproduction/test command, files/services in scope and explicit non-goals. Split work longer than a few hours or with multiple independent outcomes [S01,S05,S06].
reference_workflow.human_gate: Product/security owner approves high-impact plan; low-risk templates may auto-pass.

reference_workflow.mechanics: Create fresh container/VM/worktree at immutable SHA; install only locked dependencies in setup; inject short-lived scoped credentials; remove setup secrets before agent loop where supported; default-deny network then allowlist domains and safe HTTP methods [S10,S11,S14,S20,S24].
reference_workflow.output: environment ID, policy digest, source/dependency attestations and cost ceiling.

reference_workflow.mechanics: Agent reads repository instructions (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md or equivalent), reproduces issue, edits on a dedicated branch, runs targeted tests/linters/type checks/security checks, and records commands/diffs. Hooks/policy deny writes outside workspace, secret access, production mutation, arbitrary egress and privilege escalation [S10,S18-S21].
reference_workflow.output: signed/attributed commits, logs, evidence bundle and residual-risk notes.

reference_workflow.trigger: agent claims completion or reaches budget
reference_workflow.mechanics: Run deterministic checks outside the agent’s control, compare against acceptance tests, scan secrets/dependencies/SAST, inspect changed scope, detect flaky tests and cap repair loops. On repeated failure, stop and summarize rather than silently expand scope [S14,S15,S28].
reference_workflow.output: pass/fail matrix; failure returns to triage with artifacts.

reference_workflow.mechanics: Open a draft PR with original request, plan, change summary, test evidence, agent/model/version, environment/policy, cost, session log and rollback instructions. Independent reviewer checks design, security, behavior and generated tests; requester cannot self-approve where rules support separation [S13-S16,S24].

Rebase and rerun trusted CI with deployment credentials still unavailable to the agent. Merge only via protected branch/ruleset; deploy through normal progressive delivery, never the agent’s shell [S14].
reference_workflow.output: merge commit, build provenance and deployment candidate.

reference_workflow.mechanics: Canary, observe SLO/error/security signals and auto-rollback on deterministic thresholds. Attribute incidents to agent PRs. Feed accepted/rejected outcomes, review time, rework, escaped defects and cost into per-task-class evaluation; update prompts/policies only by reviewed change [S13,S21].
reference_workflow.output: closed task, rollback or human incident; evaluation record.

integration_points.source_control: GitHub is common to all; Codex also documents GitLab Beta, Cursor documents GitLab/Bitbucket/Azure DevOps; agents use provider apps, branches, PR/MR comments, checks and rulesets [S09,S13,S15,S19,S23,S24].
integration_points.work_intake: Issues/PR comments and agent panels; Slack, Teams, Linear and Jira depending on product; Devin v3 REST can create/poll/message/terminate sessions, while Claude Actions/SDK and Cursor API support event-driven custom flows [S03,S08,S09,S13,S19,S23].
integration_points.environment: Vendor containers/VMs, GitHub Actions ephemeral jobs, or local terminal/worktree. Pin runtime and lockfiles; put setup commands in repository-owned configuration such as AGENTS.md and scripts [S10,S13,S20,S23].
integration_points.verification: Existing unit/integration/e2e tests, formatter/linter/type checker, protected CI, CodeQL, secret scan and dependency advisory validation. Keep validation credentials separate from agent credentials [S10,S14,S15].
integration_points.tool_extensions: MCP, hooks, CLI/SDK and external APIs widen access to databases, browsers and services. Each tool needs an explicit schema, allowlist, read/write classification, audit record and rate limit [S19-S21,S23,S34].
integration_points.observability_and_finops: Session logs, signed/attributed commits, GitHub audit/PR lifecycle APIs, Devin enterprise analytics and Claude OTel usage/cost/tool telemetry can feed a control plane [S03,S13,S14,S21].
integration_points.deployment: Treat PR merge as final agent boundary. Connect only to ordinary CI/CD with protected environments, approvals, provenance, canary and rollback; no cited platform proves safe unrestricted production operation.

human_gates.required_when: user-facing behavior, vague requirements, architecture/data model, legal/licensing, destructive migration or high-cost task
human_gates.why: Agents cannot reliably infer product intent or missing constraints; ambiguity drives plausible but wrong work [S01,S05,S28].

human_gates.required_when: new network domain, dependency, secret, MCP tool, write outside branch/worktree, cloud or production action
human_gates.why: Prompt injection can convert external data into tool actions; UI confidence is not authorization [S11,S16,S18,S20,S34].

human_gates.required_when: every code-producing task; require domain/security specialist for high-risk changes
human_gates.why: GitHub explicitly makes human review mandatory for its agent, and benchmark/field evidence shows substantial incorrect output [S14,S28,S33].

human_gates.required_when: agent-authored workflow changes or code from untrusted trigger
human_gates.why: workflow code can steal credentials; GitHub therefore defaults to approve-and-run [S14].

human_gates.required_when: always for production until task-class evidence supports narrow auto-merge; always manual for auth, payments, security policy, infra, migrations and safety-critical code
human_gates.why: passing agent-written tests is not independent evidence and no platform evidence establishes full-project autonomy.

human_gates.required_when: budget/time cap, repeated same failure, expanding diff, flaky/inconclusive tests, unclear root cause, secret/injection alert or low confidence
human_gates.why: prevents Devin-style days-long pursuit of impossible paths and controls economic loss [S28].

technical: Incorrect but plausible patch; incomplete cross-cutting change; tests overfit to implementation; deleted/disabled tests; environment differs from CI/production; stale branch/merge conflict; non-deterministic tool or model behavior; context loss on large repos; failure to stop or recognize blocker [S06,S28,S33].
security: Direct/indirect prompt injection in issues, docs, web pages or dependencies; secret/code exfiltration; malicious dependency/license ingress; compromised MCP/tool; workflow-file credential theft; excessive repository/cloud permission; unsafe local command; cross-tenant persistence [S11,S14,S18,S20,S24,S34].
product_quality: Solves stated issue but violates unstated product intent, accessibility, performance, compatibility, operability or maintainability; generates code soup and review burden [S28].
organizational: Review becomes bottleneck; staff rubber-stamp large diffs; ownership/accountability unclear; agent-generated issue/PR storms; skills atrophy; vendor/model changes invalidate rules and evals [S08,S13].
measurement: Merge rate, PR count, LOC and tokens reward activity and hide selection, review/rework and escaped defects; static benchmark contamination and scaffold/budget differences mislead comparisons [S07,S31,S32].
economic: Parallel retries and long context consume credits/Actions/compute; setup and review time exceed saved implementation time; lock-in to proprietary environments/instructions; unpredictable rate limits and model retirement [S12,S15,S22,S28].
availability_and_governance: Hosted outage/queue, preview feature churn, model behavior drift, residency/retention mismatch and insufficient audit export; live Devin security docs also state default training may apply unless paid users opt out [S02,S15,S16].

controls_and_mitigations: Use provider apps/service users, repository allowlists and per-task short-lived identities. Grant one-branch push only; deny merge, deployment, admin, billing and production-data rights [S03,S14,S24].

Run in disposable containers/VMs/worktrees. Default-deny filesystem beyond workspace and network; separate setup from agent; use lockfiles, internal mirrors, domain/method allowlists, egress logs and secret removal/rotation [S10,S11,S20,S24].

Treat repository/issues/web/tool results as untrusted input. Sanitize hidden content, but assume filters are incomplete; enforce capabilities outside the model with policy-as-code and tool-level authorization [S11,S14,S16,S34].

Keep acceptance tests and final CI outside the writable agent context. Add mutation/negative tests for critical logic; block test deletion, suspicious workflow changes, new binaries, large scope growth, secrets and high/critical dependency findings [S14,S15].
Protect branches, require independent CODEOWNERS review, signed/attributed commits and a second approval for unattributed agent PRs; do not let requester/agent satisfy separation of duties [S14].

Set wall-clock, tool-call, token/credit, diff-size and retry budgets. Circuit-break repeated errors and queue pressure. Return a structured failure with attempted evidence and remaining unknowns [S03,S04,S12,S22,S28].
Log prompt/spec, source SHA, model/agent version, permissions, network/tool calls, commands, diffs, checks, costs and reviewers. Export OTel/audit metrics and retain per policy [S03,S14,S21].

Pilot per task class against a human/control baseline. Track accepted-without-major-rework rate, lead time, reviewer minutes, escaped defects, rollback/security events and total cost. Requalify on model/platform/config changes [S07,S29,S30,S32].
Use canary/progressive delivery and automatic rollback based on deterministic SLOs. Agents may propose remediation, but production write authority remains in protected deployment automation.

maturity_assessment.overall: Conditionally useful and production-usable as a supervised issue-to-PR subsystem; emerging for event-driven triage/fleets; speculative and unsafe as an end-to-end self-managing software organization.
production_ready: Low/medium-risk, well-specified, testable backlog tasks in repos with reproducible environments, mature CI and review [S01,S05,S09,S13].
Developer-steered local agents with explicit permissions/sandbox and hosted agents that produce draft PRs [S14,S18,S20,S24].
Parallel migrations, routine tests/docs and scanner-generated remediations after organization-specific pilots [S06].
emerging: Unattended scheduled/event agent runs, automated confidence-gated triage and third-party agents inside GitHub; several cited surfaces remain public preview [S15,S16].
Multi-repo and broad MCP/browser/tool access: capable but creates a larger security and review boundary [S23,S34].
not_demonstrated: Reliable autonomous requirements discovery, architecture governance, safe merge/deploy/operate loops, self-modifying policy, or sustained net ROI across representative organizations. Conflicting field and benchmark evidence prevents this conclusion [S28-S30,S32,S33].
maturity_assessment.rationale: The execution plumbing, isolation, integrations, audit and human handoff are real. Correctness predictability, adversarial robustness, economic measurement and product judgment remain limiting factors.

build_vs_buy.buy_hosted_when: Choose GitHub Copilot cloud agent if GitHub-native rules/audit/security checks and low integration effort dominate [S13-S16]. Choose Codex cloud for isolated parallel tasks and OpenAI local/cloud continuity [S09-S12]. Choose Devin for enterprise fleet/API/analytics and migration-style workflows after a task-class pilot [S03,S06-S08]. Choose Cursor Cloud Agents for Cursor-centric, multi-repo/browser/MCP workflows [S23,S24]. Jules is a simpler Google alternative [S25,S26].
build_vs_buy.build_or_self_host_when: Use Claude Code Action/SDK or OpenHands when custom triggers, provider choice, private infrastructure, bespoke tools or data residency outweigh operating cost [S19-S21,S27].
custom_engineering_still_required: task intake/risk classifier and spec templates
build_vs_buy.avoid: Do not build a new general coding agent unless control, residency or domain tooling is strategic. Do not buy based on leaderboard or demo alone; run identical private tasks with identical budgets and acceptance tests [S28-S33].

recommended_pattern.name: bounded autonomous worker, human-owned control plane
recommended_pattern.architecture: Keep issue tracker and Git as system of record. A deterministic control plane creates signed task envelopes, selects one approved agent, provisions a least-privilege ephemeral environment, enforces policy/budget, gathers evidence, and opens only a draft PR. Trusted CI, independent review, protected merge and progressive delivery remain outside the agent.
rollout: Start read-only repository Q&A/plan generation, then docs/tests, then small bug fixes, then repetitive migrations/security remediation. Never start with production access.

Build a 50–200 task private evaluation stratified by repository and risk. Compare two agents plus human baseline on acceptance, major rework, reviewer minutes, latency, total cost and escaped defects; keep failures in the dataset [S29,S30,S32].

Auto-route only task classes whose lower-confidence performance and review economics beat baseline. Retain human spec, PR and deploy gates; consider auto-merge only for reversible, generated, low-risk files after sustained evidence.
Use vendor-agnostic repository instructions and a common task/result schema. Pin models/config where possible and canary upgrades to reduce lock-in/drift.
Review monthly: accepted-without-major-rework, cycle time, review burden, cost, incidents, abort reasons and selection effects. Expand rights only through reviewed policy changes.
recommended_pattern.selection_advice: For a GitHub-first project, begin with Copilot cloud agent or Codex cloud for supervised draft PRs; add Claude Code/SDK for programmable local or CI tasks. Trial Devin only where parallel repeatable queues justify its fleet/analytics layer. Keep OpenHands as a control/self-host option. The right portfolio may use multiple workers behind one control plane rather than one agent with broad rights.
recommended_pattern.stop_condition: If reviewer time plus compute exceeds the human baseline, escaped defects rise, or injection/policy incidents occur, reduce the eligible task class or revert to developer-driven assistance.

open_questions: What are 2026 accepted-without-major-rework and escaped-defect rates for each platform on the same recent private tasks, same compute budget and same repository setup?
How much of reported merge-rate/productivity improvement comes from model progress versus task selection, better environments, user learning or increased retries [S06,S29,S30]?
Can prompt-injection resistance be independently certified when an agent reads untrusted issues, repository content, MCP output and the web [S11,S34]?

Which hosted platforms provide contractual residency, retention deletion, model-training opt-out, incident notification, complete audit export and reproducible/pinned model versions for a given organization [S02]?
What is the full cost per accepted change after setup, retries, CI, review, rework, incidents and vendor credits—not tokens or PR count [S07,S12,S15,S22]?
How stable are current 2026 preview features, pricing, quotas, GitHub partner-agent behavior and API contracts [S03,S04,S12,S15,S16]?
When, if ever, is narrow auto-merge safer than human review, and what lower-bound sample size/defect rate should authorize it?
How should ownership, licensing/provenance and accountability work when multiple vendor agents edit one PR or automatically fix each other’s findings?

confidence.overall: High for documented mechanics and security boundaries; medium for current market status/cost because live docs change and many pages are undated; low-to-medium for productivity and comparative quality because independent evidence is narrow, aging relative to 2026 and methodologically conflicted.
high: specific independent study designs and reported results [S28-S34]
medium: Product status and pricing as observed on 2026-09-13 [S04,S12,S15,S16,S25,S26]
vendor adoption, merge-rate, throughput and cost aggregates [S06-S08,S22]
low: Cross-platform ranking, current generalized success rate, net ROI, and safety of autonomous merge/deploy; no apples-to-apples 2026 independent study was found.

conflicts.conflict: Cognition reports Devin’s PR merge rate reached 67% and large deployments, while Answer.AI found only 3 successes in 20 tasks [S06,S28].
conflicts.likely_explanation: Different product generations, customer/task selection, coaching/environment maturity and outcome definitions. Merge rate excludes tasks never converted to PR and is not equivalent to correct-first-attempt success.

conflicts.conflict: METR early-2025 randomized work measured a 19% slowdown, while developers perceived speedup and the later 2025 cohort had raw speedup point estimates [S29,S30].
conflicts.likely_explanation: Rapid tool changes plus different user/task selection and concurrent-agent workflows. METR says later estimates are biased and statistically inconclusive, so neither supports a universal 2026 effect.

conflicts.conflict: SWE-bench leaderboards show rapidly rising resolution, yet SWE-Lancer’s best reported independent-coding result was 26.2% and SWE-rebench flags contamination inflation [S31-S33].
conflicts.likely_explanation: Different task distributions, freshness, hidden tests, scaffold/tool budgets and possible training contamination; benchmark scores do not measure review cost, security or operations.

conflicts.conflict: Google announced Jules was out of public beta, while its live getting-started documentation still calls it experimental [S25,S26].
conflicts.likely_explanation: “experimental” may describe capability risk rather than release phase, or documentation wording may lag; status should not be read as production assurance.

conflicts.conflict: Vendors market autonomous engineering, but their own safeguards require scoped branches, constrained networks, tests and human merge [S01,S09,S13,S14,S18,S24].
conflicts.likely_explanation: Autonomy describes execution inside a bounded task, not accountability or full SDLC authority.
